newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert pledges understanding for SKET.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert pledges understanding for SKET.

text.p: The European Commission will show understanding for a new restructuring plan for German machinery giant SKET GmbH, Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert was quoted as telling a delegation of SKET's workers on Wednesday.
The former east German company went into liquidation proceedings last week after its 1,850 workforce refused to support a cost-cutting programme under which two-thirds of them would lose their jobs.

"Van Miert stressed that he was concerned with the situation...and that he would analyse the plan with the same understanding he has already shown for the SKET case," his spokesman quoted him as saying. Van Miert had met earlier on Wednesday with a delegation of SKET's workers' council.
But he recalled that as a general rule, the new rescue plan must ensure the return of the company to viability, the spokesman said.

The Commission in March 1995 started a probe into 957.1 million marks ($627.4 million) of state aid covering the waiving of shareholders credits, loan guarantees and other financial assistance for the troubled company. Part of it aimed to cover for losses during a previous restructuring period between 1994 and 1996.
Van Miert's spokesman declined to put an exact figure on additional help given to SKET since March 1995, saying it was in the order of tens of millions of marks.

The Commission's suspicion that this represented operating aid had been contested by the workers' representatives, he said. They also denied allegations that the company was dumping on the machinery market.
German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said earlier this week in Brussels that a new rescue plan for the struggling east German machinery maker would be submitted within six to eight weeks.
The company is currently under the authority of the BvS state agency charged with the task of privatising the former east German economy.
